It really depends on who you are and what you're trying to do. Tachyon's base power is a pretty good way of getting extra burst cards into her trash while increasing her chances of drawing cards that she actually wants. Blindly drawing an extra card doesn't help you to get burst cards into your trash faster, if you don't have a way to increase your number of card plays.

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
A basic comparison between base Tachyon and TLT. This assumes that every turn, Tachyon plays 1 one-shot, uses her power to discard the top card of her deck, and then draws one card. TLT plays 1 one-shot, uses her power to draw a card, and then draws a second card.

Hand/Trash      Tachyon        TLT
Start:                  4/0            4/0
After turn 1:        4/2            5/1
After turn 2:        4/4            6/2
After turn 3:        4/6            7/3
After turn 4:        4/8            8/4
...
After turn 10:     4/20          14/10

Obviously, this is a bit simplistic, since a lot of her cards allow you to play/draw extra cards. But both versions of Tachyon have access to those. Team Leader Tachyon sacrifices the ability to put extra cards directly into her trash for the ability to put extra cards directly into her hand. She definitely has more cards to play, but does not have a greater ability to play cards than original Tachyon. Additionally, if original Tachyon can get Research Grant into play, she'll put cards into her trash just as quickly as with her base power AND build up her hand as quickly as TLT.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I posted this over there, but I think the review really captures the strongest weakness of the App, and that is players that are new to Sentinels when they get the app.

 

Even a good tutorial on how to play the game isn't going to help you learn the heroes, and playing Sentinels solo is a horrible way to learn the game.

Second to that an app will never put the physical deck in your hand where you can look through the deck, pair up cards and get a real feeling for how the deck should work.

When you play the game with no experience, controlling 4 heroes against a Villain you don't know and an environment you don't know you end up with reactions like the review had.  Things like:

Damage is all that matters.

X hero is worthless, or X hero is the best ever.

Fanatic is a healer!  (I've read three different reviews that said that one)

This game needs a healer!

and my favorite:

This game lacks strategy or meaningful choices.

 

There isn't an easy solution to this, things like a deck viewer might help, but not like having cards in your hand, and the implementation probably isn't worth it for the amount of value it would add.  Tutorials for each hero would be ridiculous and eat so much space, the best way to learn is to play one hero several times with your friends.

This app is amazing for people who love Sentinels and want to play it when they wouldn't be able to normally. because it takes away the work of playing solo, does the fiddlyness for you, which gives you a chance to play SotM on your lunch break or on the bus or a road trip, it is awesome.  The implementation is superb from what I've seen so far.

I'm sure we will get some people who see the beauty of the game and slog through the learning process on the app to really get to know the game, but overall the card game with people who know the game already is a far superior introduction.

She definitely has more cards to play, but does not have a greater ability to play cards than original Tachyon. Additionally, if original Tachyon can get Research Grant into play, she'll put cards into her trash just as quickly as with her base power AND build up her hand as quickly as TLT.

This isn't a really good model, since this ensures that you're guaranteed to dump a one-shot.

But I think you're underestimating the impressive hand resources that TLT has, the exact point I'm trying to make. Statistically, the more you draw the higher chance you have of discarding more cards anyway. You draw into power cards like HUD Goggles and Pushing the Limits quicker, and then proceeding to utilize Fleet of Foot and Quick Insight. A total of five cards in her deck between those names alone, which are also bursts (again, allowing your entire team to benefit). Yes, they share the same deck, but in this case her hand is the better resource. What if you don't reveal a burst with Tachyon? It's a dead card toward your strategy, and goes to your hand anyway.

I just think Tachyon as opposed to TLT is slower and riskier. At least it seems that way to me.

posts.cooked: For those of us who aren't too familiar with the process behind Greenlight, how many votes do we need before it gets approved to make it to the shop?

posts.name: BenjaminTodd
posts.cooked:
There's no fixed number.  From the Steam FAQ:

How many votes does a game need to get selected?

The specific number of votes doesn't matter as much as relative interest in a game compared with other games in Steam Greenlight—we need customers to help us prioritize which games they want to see made available on Steam.

 

Basically, they prioritized based on the interest of the games in comparison to others.  So if SotM:TVG (is that a thing yet?) gets 1000 votes, but the average is 5000, it receives lower priority.  If SotM:TVG get 10000 and the average is 5000, it receives higher priority.  I'm sure there are also a host of other factors involved like developer commitment, market potential, and a others things that help the game get chosen.

But in then end, lots of votes make it easier for it to be greenlit.

Carlos
